overview: This 446-page file traces Japanese naval transports’ requests to visit California and Hawaiian ports from 1940 into 1941. Diplomatic notes, agency correspondence, and naval reports document shifting port restrictions, oil-loading visits, disputes over public-vessel privileges, and growing security and export-control concerns.
interest: It shows how routine port courtesies became contested through oil exports, vessel-status disputes, and reports of suspected intelligence gathering.
